title: Stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers stereotypes and prejudice but defines prejudice as a judgement about a person, not a negative attitude toward a group, and it does not teach discrimination as a third idea, so it is related rather than the same point.

draft.title: Stereotypes, prejudice and discrimination
card: Stereotype
a belief about the traits of a group, applied to its members as if they were all the same. It is the thinking part.
Prejudice
a negative attitude toward a group and its members, based on group membership. It is the feeling part.
Discrimination
treating people unfairly because of the group they belong to. It is the behaviour part.
The three often link: a stereotype can feed prejudice, and prejudice can lead to discrimination. But a person can hold a stereotype and never act on it.
draft.remember: Stereotype is a belief, prejudice is a feeling, discrimination is an action.

a.q: Which of these is an example of discrimination?
opts: A manager refuses to interview applicants over 60
A man believes older workers are bad with computers
A woman dislikes older workers without knowing any
A student thinks all older workers are set in their ways
a.why: Refusing to interview someone because of their age is unfair treatment, so it is behaviour. The other options describe beliefs or feelings, which are stereotypes or prejudice until someone acts on them.
a.clue: Which option is something a person does, not thinks or feels?

b.q: Priya says, "Teenagers are lazy," then happily hires a keen 16-year-old for her shop. Which statement fits best?
opts: She holds a stereotype but did not discriminate
She is prejudiced and also discriminated
She discriminated but holds no stereotype
She holds neither a stereotype nor a prejudice
b.why: Saying teenagers are lazy is a belief about a group, so it is a stereotype. She hired the teenager and treated them fairly, so she did not discriminate. A stereotype does not always lead to unfair action.
b.clue: Check what she believes, then check what she actually did.

a.best: A manager refuses to interview applicants over 60

b.best: She holds a stereotype but did not discriminate

problems.detail: The option 'She is prejudiced and also discriminated' is ungrammatical and ambiguous. 'Discriminated' could be read as 'was discriminated against'. Reword to 'She is prejudiced and also discriminated against teenagers' or 'She is prejudiced and also acted unfairly'.

check.summary: The content is accurate and both intended answers are correct. One distractor in question b is awkwardly worded and could be read as 'was discriminated against'.
